settings.title: Settings
settings.languageHint: Invoices can be printed in a different language from the app.
settings.businessHint: Printed on invoices. GSTIN and state decide how tax is charged.
settings.registrationHint: Composition and unregistered businesses issue a bill of supply without GST.
settings.readOnly: Your role can view but not change these.
settings.stockPolicyHint: When a bill needs more than the stock in hand
settings.creditLimitHint: When a bill takes a customer over their limit
settings.overdueHint: When a customer has bills past their due date
settings.printLanguageHint: Default language for printed and shared invoices
settings.allocationHint: How a payment is applied when no bill is chosen
settings.expiryWarningHint: Warn about batches expiring within this many days
settings.seriesHint: Invoice, purchase and receipt numbering per financial year
settings.patternHint: Use {SEQ:4} for the running number and {FY} for the year, e.g. INV/{FY}/{SEQ:4}. GST allows up to 16 characters.
settings.termsHint: Printed at the foot of every invoice, e.g. return policy, interest on late payment, jurisdiction. Saved when you leave the box.
settings.logoHint: Printed at the top of bills, receipts, notes and slips, and shown in the menu. PNG, JPG or WebP; a logo on a white or clear background looks best.
settings.logoPreview: How bills will show your firm
settings.accentHint: The app's main colour: buttons, the menu and highlights. Paid, due and overdue keep their own colours.
settings.offlineWipeHint: Days without connecting (0 = never). A phone or PC that stays offline longer deletes its saved copy; work waiting on it is sent at the next sign-in. A device you remove in the list below deletes its copy as soon as it connects.
settings.lutHint: For exports and supplies to SEZ without paying IGST. Filed each financial year on the GST portal (form RFD-11). Leave empty if you have none.

statutory.title: Salary: PF, ESI and professional tax
statutory.hint: Worked out on every salary slip instead of entered by hand. Check the rates with your accountant.
statutory.savedHint: Recalculate a draft payroll to use it.

pfWagesOptions.codes: Labour codes: basic + DA, at least half the pay

pfWagesHint.codes: Code on Social Security, 2020: allowances above half the pay count as wages

statutory.ceiling: Contribute on at most ₹15,000 a month (the wage ceiling)

statutory.ptOn: Professional tax on the month's gross pay
statutory.ptBuiltIn: Built-in slabs for {{state}}. Change them if your state's notification differs.

settings.ewayThresholdHint: ₹50,000 in most states; some states set more for movement within the state
settings.paymentDetailsHint: Printed on invoices: the bank account and UPI ID. Bills that still owe money also get a UPI code to scan, on the PDF and on receipts.
settings.billUnitsHint: Each line of a bill has a list of the units the product is sold in (pieces, strips, boxes). Typing a unit's letter after the quantity picks it: 2 then B is 2 boxes. A letter two units share picks one, then the other.

general.s1: The menu on the left (on a phone, the Menu button) opens every screen your role allows.
general.s2: Search at the top (Ctrl+K) finds any customer, product or bill by name, mobile or number.
general.s3: The + button (Ctrl+I on a computer) starts a new bill from anywhere.
general.s4: The Aa button makes the text bigger or the menu simpler.

dashboard.s1: The top cards show today's sales, money to collect and stock to reorder.
dashboard.s2: Tap a card to open the list behind it.
dashboard.s3: Quick actions start a bill, a payment or a new customer in one tap.
dashboard.s4: Each role sees its own work here: a salesman sees his beat, the accountant sees dues.

invoices.s1: Choose the customer (F3) by name or mobile. A new shop can be added right from the search.
invoices.s2: Type a product (F2), press Enter, type the quantity, Enter, check the rate, Enter for the next item.
invoices.s3: Save with Ctrl+S. The popup offers Send on WhatsApp, Print and New invoice.
invoices.s4: Ctrl+P saves and prints in one step.

bills.s1: All sales bills, newest first. Filter by date, customer or status (paid, part paid, due).
bills.s2: Open a bill to print it, send it on WhatsApp, copy it or cancel it.
bills.s3: Totals of the filtered bills are at the top; the download button saves the list as CSV.

customers.s1: Add customer saves the shop's name, mobile, GSTIN, credit limit and price list.
customers.s2: Open a customer for their bills, payments and ledger.
customers.s3: Import brings a whole customer list in from Excel or CSV.

payments.s1: Receive payment (Alt+C): pick the customer, the amount and how they paid (cash, UPI, cheque).
payments.s2: The payment is set against their oldest bills on its own; you can change that.
payments.s3: Send the receipt on WhatsApp from the payment.

outstanding.s1: Every customer who owes money, with how long it has been due.
outstanding.s2: Open a customer to send them a reminder on WhatsApp.
outstanding.s3: Their unpaid bills and the oldest due date are shown there too.

products.s1: Add product: name, HSN, GST rate, unit, selling price and MRP.
products.s2: Import brings a whole price list in from Excel, CSV or PDF.
products.s3: Price B and Price C are rates for wholesale and other customer lists.

inventory.s1: Stock of every product in every godown.
inventory.s2: Stock adjustment corrects stock after counting or damage.
inventory.s3: Low stock shows what to order again.

purchases.s1: New purchase bill brings stock in from a supplier.
purchases.s2: Import bill reads the supplier's Excel, CSV or PDF bill for you.
purchases.s3: Items not in your product list can be added in one go from the bill.

suppliers.s1: Add a supplier with GSTIN and mobile.
suppliers.s2: Open a supplier for their purchase bills and what you owe them.

orders.s1: A sales order records what a shop wants before you bill it.
orders.s2: Turn an order into a bill in one click when the goods go out.

gst.s1: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B are made from your bills and purchases.
gst.s2: Download the files for the GST portal, or give them to your CA.
gst.s3: Check the warnings first: a missing GSTIN or HSN shows there.

expenses.s1: Record shop expenses: rent, electricity, fuel, salaries paid in cash.
expenses.s2: They show in profit and in the day's cash.

reports.s1: Sales, profit, stock and collections by day, week or month.
reports.s2: Every report downloads as PDF or Excel.

settings.s1: Business profile: your firm's name, address, GSTIN and logo for every bill.
settings.s2: Open on phone shows a QR code to open Digital Bahi on a phone on the same Wi-Fi.
settings.s3: Bill numbers, price lists, godowns and WhatsApp are set up here too.

users.s1: Add member: name, mobile, role, and a user ID and password if they should sign in straight away.
users.s2: After adding, Send invite on WhatsApp sends them the link and their user ID.
users.s3: A role decides which screens a person sees.

backup.s1: Download backup saves your whole book in one file. Give it a password and write it down.
backup.s2: Automatic backups make a copy every day by themselves.
backup.s3: Restore always makes a new business: your current one is never touched.

twoStep.title: Two-step sign-in
twoStep.subtitle: After your password or OTP, a code from an authenticator app on your phone. Someone who learns your password still cannot get in.
twoStep.offHelp: Turn it on for the owner and anyone who handles money or settings. It takes a minute: you need an authenticator app such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator.
twoStep.fewCodes: Few recovery codes left. Make new ones and keep them safe.
twoStep.stepInstall: Install an authenticator app on your phone (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or another).
twoStep.stepScan: In the app, add an account and scan this QR code.
twoStep.stepCode: Type the 6-digit code the app shows.
twoStep.qrLabel: QR code to add Digital Bahi to an authenticator app
twoStep.cantScan: Can't scan it? Type this key in the app instead:
twoStep.openApp: The app is on this phone? Open it here
twoStep.useRecovery: Lost your phone? Use a recovery code
twoStep.useApp: Use the code from the app instead
twoStep.codesHelp: If you lose your phone, each of these recovery codes signs you in once instead of the app's code. Keep them somewhere safe, away from your phone: they are shown only now.
twoStep.codesFileTitle: Digital Bahi recovery codes (each works once)
twoStep.keptCodes: I have kept these codes safe
twoStep.newCodesHelp: Type a code from the app (or a recovery code). The old recovery codes stop working.
twoStep.newCodesDone: Your new recovery codes. The old ones no longer work.
twoStep.offWarning: Your password (or an OTP) alone will open your account again. If your business asks for two-step sign-in, it stays closed to you until you turn it back on.
twoStep.signInHelp: Open the authenticator app on your phone and type the 6-digit code for Digital Bahi.
twoStep.lostPhone: Lost your phone and your recovery codes? Ask the business owner to turn two-step sign-in off for you.
twoStep.expired: That took a while, so sign in again.
twoStep.requiredHelp: Before the business opens, turn it on: from now on, after your password or OTP you will also type a code from an authenticator app on your phone.
twoStep.settingsHint: Members of the roles ticked must sign in with a code from an authenticator app as well. Until they turn it on (in My profile), the business stays closed to them.
twoStep.settingsOwnerNote: To ask it of your own role (Admin), turn it on for yourself first in My profile.
twoStep.settingsOnlyOwner: Only the owner can change this.
